parameters.excerpt: Implementations might provide anywhere from 1 to 3 privilege modes trading off reduced isolation for lower implementation cost.
parameters.reasoning: The number of privilege modes (1 to 3) is an implementation choice that affects system design. It is not controlled by any CSR field.

parameters.excerpt: Each privilege level has a core set of privileged ISA extensions with optional extensions and variants.
parameters.reasoning: The specific extensions and variants supported at each privilege level are implementation-defined choices, allowing flexibility in design.

parameters.excerpt: Implementations may also include a debug mode to support off-chip debugging and/or manufacturing test.
parameters.reasoning: Whether to include a debug mode is an implementation choice, making it a direct parameter of the architecture.

skipped_non_parameters.excerpt: The machine level has the highest privileges and is the only mandatory privilege level for a RISC-V hardware platform.
skipped_non_parameters.reason: This is a fixed requirement that all implementations must satisfy, not an implementation choice.

skipped_non_parameters.excerpt: The lock feature of the optional PMP facility can provide some limited protection even with only M-mode implemented.
skipped_non_parameters.reason: This describes a feature of the PMP facility, not an implementation-defined parameter.

skipped_non_parameters.excerpt: A hart normally runs application code in U-mode until some trap (e.g., a supervisor call or a timer interrupt) forces a switch to a trap handler.
skipped_non_parameters.reason: This describes runtime behavior and not an implementation choice regarding privilege levels.

skipped_non_parameters.excerpt: Horizontal traps can be implemented as vertical traps that return control to a horizontal trap handler in the less-privileged mode.
